name: Gurugram Tech Employee Unpaid Salary & Relieving Letter Withheld
raw_input: I worked as a frontend developer at an IT consultancy firm in Cyber City, Gurugram for 18 months at Rs 70,000/month. I submitted my resignation on 1st August 2024 and completed my full 60-day notice period till 30th September 2024. All project handovers and company assets (MacBook, ID card) were handed over and I received an asset clearance certificate from IT. My August salary was delayed, and my September salary plus 15 days encashable leave (total Rs 1,65,000) has not been paid. It has been 50 days since my last working day. Whenever I email HR, they say 'finance team is facing client payment delays'. More importantly, they are withholding my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate. My new employer is threatening to cancel my job offer if I don't submit my relieving letter by end of this week. I have my appointment letter, resignation acceptance email, and signed clearance form.

case_dossier.case_title: Withheld Salary and Service Certificates Dispute
case_dossier.summary: An ex-frontend developer completed a 60-day notice period at an IT firm in Gurugram on 30th September 2024 after 18 months of service. The employer has withheld the August and September salary along with 15 days encashable leave totaling Rs 1,65,000, as well as the Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate, endangering a new job offer.
case_dossier.opposite_party: IT Consultancy Firm, Cyber City, Gurugram

timeline.event: Submitted resignation to the IT consultancy firm.
Completed full 60-day notice period, handed over project assets and ID card, and received asset clearance certificate from IT.
Repeated follow-ups via email regarding unpaid August salary, September salary, and encashable leave, to which HR replied citing client payment delays.

evidence_held: Emails with HR regarding payment delays
evidence_needed: Bank statements showing past salary credits
Employment contract detailing notice period and leave encashment terms
Written communication from the new employer regarding the threat to cancel the job offer
case_dossier.evidence_strength_explanation: Strong documentary proof of employment, resignation acceptance, and formal clearance exists, though final pay slips and bank statements should be compiled.

escalation_check.legal_aid_contact: District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Toll-Free Helpline: 15100

rights_advice.plain_language_standing:
You are well within your legal rights to demand your full and final settlement from your former employer after completing your notice period. Under Indian labor law, unpaid wages upon resignation must be settled promptly, and withholding earned compensation is a civil matter rather than a criminal one. Your strong documentary evidence, including your resignation acceptance and clearance form, puts you in a solid position to seek your dues.

The Code on Wages, 2019 protects your right to receive your final wages within the legally mandated timeframe following your separation from the company. By following the proper pre-litigation and administrative channels, you can systematically pursue your unpaid salary and leave encashment without needing to resort to inappropriate police complaints.

Take immediate action by issuing a formal written demand to your former employer citing the relevant wage code, and prepare to approach the competent labor authority if they fail to comply within a reasonable period.

governing_laws.relevance: States that the wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within two working days of that event.

governing_laws.act_name: General Legal Principle (Civil vs. Criminal Boundary)
governing_laws.relevance: Establishes that failure to pay wages is a civil dispute or breach of contract rather than criminal cheating, meaning you should pursue labor authorities rather than police complaints.

action_options.title: Immediate Pre-Litigation Action (Formal Legal Notice / Email)
action_options.details: Send a formal written demand email to your former employer citing Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, requesting immediate release of your unpaid wages within two working days. For your relieving or experience letters, note that no fixed legal deadline is stated in the statute; check your contract and company policy, or consult a lawyer. Do not file criminal police complaints as this is a civil monetary dispute.

action_options.title: Statutory Authority / Grievance Portal Filing
action_options.details: For formal proceedings or recovery of unpaid wages, approach the competent labour authority (confirm locally). Remember that the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) / NALSA Helpline 15100 provides free legal aid and guidance only, and is never a forum for hearings or proceedings against an employer.

action_options.title: Statutory Forum / Labor Petition
action_options.details: If the employer fails to respond to your written demands or the labor authority conciliation does not resolve the issue, consult with the competent labor authority or a legal professional to file a formal claim for your remaining dues.

rights_advice.real_lawyer_guidance: Since this dispute involves potential threats to a new job offer and a significant withheld amount, consulting a licensed advocate or utilizing free guidance from the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA Helpline 15100) is strongly advised to draft a formal legal notice and navigate the labor authority proceedings effectively.
rights_advice.disclaimer: ⚠️ NyayaMitra provides legal information and self-advocacy tools under Indian laws. For formal courtroom representation, consult a licensed advocate.

### LEGAL NOTICE DRAFT – REVIEW BEFORE SENDING DRAFT – REVIEW BEFORE SENDING

**FROM:**
[Your Name] 
[Your Address] 
Phone: [Your Phone Number] 
Email: [Your Email Address] 

**DATE:** 09/11/2026

**MODE OF DISPATCH:** Speed Post with Acknowledgement Due (AD) & Registered Email

**TO:**
IT Consultancy Firm, 
Cyber City, 
Gurugram, 
Haryana 

---

**SUBJECT: LEGAL NOTICE FOR WITHHOLDING DUES, UNPAID SALARY, LEAVE ENCASHMENT, AND SERVICE CERTIFICATES**

Dear Sir/Madam,

I, [Your Name], residing at [Your Address], do hereby issue this formal legal demand notice to you, the management of the IT Consultancy Firm located at Cyber City, Gurugram, calling upon you to clear my outstanding dues and release my professional service documents immediately, as detailed hereunder:

### I hereby state and submit as under:

1. That I was employed with your firm as a Frontend Developer and faithfully completed 18 months of service, discharging my professional responsibilities to the satisfaction of the management.
2. That on 1st August 2024, I formally submitted my resignation to the IT consultancy firm, providing the full contractual notice period.
3. That on 30th September 2024, I completed my full 60-day notice period, successfully handed over all project assets and my ID card, and obtained a signed asset clearance certificate from the IT department.
4. That despite the successful and clean separation, you have wrongfully withheld my salary for the month of August 2024, my salary for the month of September 2024, and 15 days of encashable leave, totaling an amount of Rs. 1,65,000 (Rupees One Lakh Sixty-Five Thousand Only).
5. That in addition to withholding my earned wages, you have also withheld my Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate, despite repeated follow-ups over the past 50 days where your HR department merely cited client payment delays as an excuse for non-payment.
6. That the withholding of my statutory dues and essential service certificates is causing severe financial distress and is endangering my new job offer, which constitutes an untenable withholding of earned compensation.
7. That under Section 17(2) of the Code on Wages, 2019, the wages of an employee who resigns must be paid within the statutory timeline. Furthermore, withholding earned remuneration upon lawful separation constitutes a civil dispute regarding breach of contract and unpaid dues.

### DEMAND FOR RECTIFICATION

Therefore, through this notice, I call upon you to settle my full and final dues amounting to **Rs. 1,65,000** along with my **Relieving Letter and Experience Certificate** within a suggested 15-day period (customary pre-litigation practice) from the receipt of this notice.

Please note that if you fail to disburse the said amount and release my service certificates within the stipulated timeframe, I shall be constrained to initiate formal legal proceedings by approaching the competent labour authority (confirm locally) and taking further legal action under the applicable laws, holding your establishment liable for all attendant costs and consequences. 

*(Note: For free legal guidance or aid regarding this matter, the District Legal Services Authority / NALSA Helpline is 15100).*

Sincerely / Yours faithfully,

*(Signature)* 
[Your Name] 

---

### ANNEXURE INVENTORY
1. Copy of Appointment Letter
2. Copy of Resignation Acceptance Email
3. Copy of Signed Asset Clearance Form
4. Copies of correspondence / emails with HR regarding payment delays

sample_roleplay_turn.user_argument: Under employment laws, full and final dues must be cleared timely and withholding my relieving letter violates my right to livelihood. If my Rs 1,65,000 and relieving letter are not issued within 3 days, I will file a formal complaint with the District Labor Commissioner.

opponent_response.opponent_reply: Arre bhai, don't throw empty threats at us with District Labor Commissioner and all! Read your employment agreement properly—Clause 14 clearly says clearance depends on project handover and management discretion. Company policy is final, and our HR head is on leave till next week anyway. Don't disturb us unnecessarily.

coach_evaluation.what_went_well: You firmly demanded your pending dues and relieving letter, and set a clear 3-day deadline while highlighting the threat to your livelihood.
coach_evaluation.what_to_improve: You mentioned vague 'employment laws' without citing any specific provisions from the Code on Wages, 2019 regarding timely payment of wages, or the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 for deficient service.
coach_evaluation.suggested_next_counter: Under the Code on Wages, 2019, earned wages must be paid promptly, and withholding them along with my relieving letter is legally untenable.
